Now when Job’s three friends— Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite— heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
Then Job replied:

verses.text: “If one ventures a word with you, will you be wearied? Yet who can keep from speaking?

xrefs.text: For I am full of words, and my spirit within me compels me.
For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.

But I am full of the LORD’s wrath; I am tired of holding it back. “Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together. For both husband and wife will be captured, the old and the very old alike.
If I say, “I will not mention Him or speak any more in His name,” His message becomes a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones, and I become weary of holding it in, and I cannot prevail.
For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.

verses.text: Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.

xrefs.text: Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!
But I would encourage you with my mouth, and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.
Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.
But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.

verses.text: Your words have steadied those who stumbled; you have braced the knees that were buckling.

xrefs.text: The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down.
Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.
And we urge you, brothers, to admonish the unruly, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone.
Speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

verses.text: But now trouble has come upon you, and you are weary. It strikes you, and you are dismayed.

xrefs.text: Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.
But stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”

xrefs.text: Do not be deceived: God is not to be mocked. Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return.

“Your ways and deeds have brought this upon you. This is your punishment; how bitter it is, because it pierces to the heart!”

xrefs.text: After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a still, small voice.

verses.text: ‘Can a mortal be more righteous than God, or a man more pure than his Maker?

xrefs.text: “Yes, I know that it is so, but how can a mortal be righteous before God?
How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
Surely there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins.
Do not bring Your servant into judgment, for no one alive is righteous before You.

verses.text: If God puts no trust in His servants, and He charges His angels with error,

xrefs.text: If even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not pure in His sight,

And the angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling— these He has kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment on that great day.
If God puts no trust in His holy ones, if even the heavens are not pure in His eyes,
